metaDescription: Six full motion TV wall mounts compared on TV size and weight limits, VESA range, tilt and swivel, extension, stud spacing, UL listing and install effort.
expertTake: The ECHOGEAR MaxMotion is our top pick because its listing states a UL listing, a 125 lb limit for 42 to 90 in TVs, a heavy-duty steel frame and a drilling template for a roughly 30 minute install. The Mounting Dream 32 to 70 in mount is the value pick for mid-size TVs, with a stated 110 lb limit. Skip the category if you cannot find studs, because a full motion arm adds leverage that a drywall anchor cannot hold safely.
introParagraphs: A full motion TV mount holds the TV on an arm that extends from the wall, swivels left and right and tilts up and down, so you can angle the screen toward a sofa, a corner or a kitchen. The same arm that gives you flexibility also puts the TV's weight out from the wall, which multiplies the load on the fasteners. That makes the studs behind the plate, the weight rating and the arm length the most important parts of the choice.

We evaluated each mount from its published specifications and patterns in owner feedback, not from installing it. Listings differ in whether they state UL listing, stud spacing and tilt range, and we say so where a figure is missing. The lineup spans small, mid-size and large TV mounts so you can match the arm to your TV and your wall.

products.name: ECHOGEAR MaxMotion Full Motion TV Wall Mount for 42 to 90 in TVs, 125 lb, UL Listed

specList.label: Install
specList.value: Under 30 minutes with a drilling template

products.description:
The ECHOGEAR MaxMotion is a full motion TV wall mount for 42 to 90 in TVs rated to 125 lb, UL listed, with a heavy-duty steel frame, a design to fit almost any VESA pattern and a drilling template and hardware kit that the listing says allows an install in under 30 minutes. The listing says it swivels, tilts and extends. It is the best-documented mount in the lineup on listing and install.

The tradeoff is leverage. A fully extended arm with a 90 in TV puts heavy torque on the wall, so a stud mount into solid framing is essential, and a UL listing does not replace checking your wall. A 125 lb limit is below the 132 lb of some rivals. Compared with the Perlegear, it is slightly lower in capacity and more documented on install.

Find the studs, use the template and check that the mount is level before hanging the TV. It suits a living room with a large TV on a stud wall where the screen needs to turn toward a sofa.
products.bestFor: Living rooms with a large TV on a stud wall that needs to turn toward the sofa.
pros: UL listing and a 125 lb limit are stated clearly
Heavy-duty steel frame suits large 42 to 90 in TVs
Drilling template and hardware kit speed installation
Full motion arm swivels, tilts and extends for flexible viewing
cons: Fully extended arm with a large TV puts heavy torque on the wall
125 lb limit is slightly lower than some rivals

products.name: Perlegear UL Listed Full Motion TV Wall Mount for 42 to 90 in TVs, 132 lb, Dual Articulating Arms

specList.label: Arms
specList.value: Dual articulating with steel bearings and washers

products.description:
The Perlegear is a UL listed full motion TV wall mount for 42 to 90 in flat and curved TVs rated to 132 lb, with dual articulating arms, solid steel bearings and precision washers at every joint. The listing says it is built for stability and lets you view from any angle. It is the highest-rated mount in the lineup by a small margin.

The tradeoff is bulk and leverage. A heavy-duty mount is itself heavy and thick, so it sits farther from the wall when folded, and a 132 lb TV at full extension is a large load on the studs. The listing asks you to check TV size and VESA before buying. Compared with the ECHOGEAR, it has a higher stated limit and less detail on install.

Use two people and a stud finder and check the VESA pattern. It suits a large TV in a living room where a high-capacity mount and a UL listing matter.
products.bestFor: Large TVs that need a high-capacity UL listed mount on a stud wall.
pros: 132 lb limit is the highest rating in the lineup
UL listing is stated on the product
Solid steel bearings and washers at each joint reduce wobble
Fits flat and curved TVs from 42 to 90 in
cons: Heavy and thick mount sits farther from the wall when folded
A heavy TV at full extension loads the studs heavily

products.name: USX Mount Full Motion TV Wall Mount for 42 to 90 in TVs, 132 lb, +5/-15 Tilt, 45 Degree Swivel
products.description:
The USX Mount is a full motion TV wall mount for 42 to 90 in TVs rated to 132 lb with dual articulating arms, a tilt of +5 to -15 degrees, a swivel of 45 degrees each way and a VESA range starting at 200 by 100 mm. The listing says all hardware comes in pre-labeled bags. It is the most affordable large-TV mount in the lineup.

The tradeoff is documentation. The text we reviewed does not state a UL listing, and swivel and tilt ranges are modest compared with the extended arms of some rivals. A budget mount may have rougher joints that creak or settle. Compared with the Perlegear, it has the same limit with fewer stated safety details.

Tighten every bolt, level the mount and check it after a week. It suits a large TV in a bedroom or living room where a high rating at a low price is wanted.
products.bestFor: Large TVs in bedrooms or living rooms that want a high rating at a modest price.
pros: 132 lb limit matches the highest in the lineup
+5 to -15 degree tilt reduces glare from windows
45 degree swivel each way gives wide angle changes
Pre-labeled hardware bags simplify installation
cons: Listing text does not state a UL listing
Budget joints can creak or settle and need re-tightening

products.name: Mounting Dream Full Motion TV Wall Mount for 32 to 70 in TVs, 110 lb, Tilt +5/-15, VESA 400x400

specList.label: Swivel
specList.value: Wide range, plus 3 degree post-install leveling

products.description:
The Mounting Dream is a full motion TV wall mount for 32 to 70 in TVs rated to 110 lb with a maximum VESA of 400 by 400 mm, a tilt of +5 to -15 degrees and a swivel, plus a plus-or-minus 3 degree level adjustment after installation. The listing says hardware comes in pre-labeled bags. It is the best match in the lineup for a 55 to 65 in TV.

The tradeoff is the VESA cap and limit. A 400 by 400 mm cap excludes the largest TVs and a 110 lb limit is lower than the large-TV mounts. The listing does not state a UL listing in the text we reviewed. Compared with the Pipishell, it has a higher limit and a defined VESA cap.

Check the TV's VESA pattern is no larger than 400 by 400 and find the studs. It suits a living room or a bedroom with a 40 to 65 in TV where a straightforward full motion mount is wanted.
products.bestFor: Living rooms and bedrooms with a 40 to 65 in TV that want a straightforward full motion mount.
pros: 32 to 70 in range matches most common TV sizes
110 lb limit suits TVs up to about 65 in
Plus or minus 3 degree level adjustment after install fixes a crooked mount
Stated 400 by 400 mm VESA cap makes fit easy to check
cons: 400 by 400 mm VESA cap excludes the largest TVs
Listing text does not state a UL listing

products.name: Pipishell Full Motion TV Wall Mount for 26 to 74 in TVs, 99 lb, Fits 12 and 16 in Studs

specList.label: Studs
specList.value: Fits 12 and 16 in wood stud spacing

products.description:
The Pipishell is a full motion TV wall mount for 26 to 74 in TVs rated to 99 lb, with dual articulating arms of heavy-gauge steel, a tilt of +5 to -15 degrees and a design that fits 12 in and 16 in wood stud spacing. The listing tells you to confirm the TV size and VESA before buying. It is the most flexible mount on stud layout in the lineup.

The tradeoff is the rating. A 99 lb limit is lower than the 110 to 132 lb mounts, which suits most TVs up to about 65 in but leaves less margin for a big set, and the listing mentions 74 in as a maximum size. The text we reviewed gives no UL listing. Compared with the Mounting Dream, it is more stud-flexible and lower in capacity.

Use a stud finder and check both stud spacings. It suits a small to mid-size TV on a wall where studs are 12 in or 16 in apart.
products.bestFor: Small to mid-size TVs on walls with 12 in or 16 in stud spacing.
pros: Fits 12 in and 16 in stud spacing, which covers common walls
26 to 74 in range covers small and large TVs
Heavy-gauge steel dual arms are described as strong
+5 to -15 degree tilt reduces glare
cons: 99 lb limit leaves less margin for large TVs

products.name: Amazon Basics Full Motion Articulating TV Wall Mount for 26 to 55 in TVs, up to 80 lb

specList.label: Wall
specList.value: Concrete, brick and wood stud, single stud

products.description:
The Amazon Basics mount is a full motion articulating TV wall mount for 26 to 55 in flat panels up to 80 lb with a VESA range from 3.9 by 3.9 to 15.7 by 15.7 in and single-stud mounting, designed for concrete, brick and wood stud walls. The listing says it supports swivel and tilt. It is the simplest and the lowest-rated mount in the lineup.

The tradeoff is the single-stud design. A mount fixed to one stud has less lateral stability than a two-stud plate, and an 80 lb limit suits small and mid-size TVs only. The listing says the 22 to 55 in range in one line and 26 to 55 in another, so check the size for your TV. Compared with the Pipishell, it is a smaller arm and a lower rating.

Use the stud finder and confirm the TV is under 80 lb including the soundbar. It suits a bedroom or a kitchen TV where a simple articulating arm is enough.

Single-stud mounting suits walls with limited studs
Works on concrete, brick and wood stud walls per the listing
Simple design is easy to understand and install
cons: Single-stud mounting is less stable laterally than a two-stud plate

buyingCriteria.explanation: The ECHOGEAR lists 125 lb, the Perlegear and USX 132 lb, the Mounting Dream 110 lb, the Pipishell 99 lb and the Amazon Basics 80 lb. A TV's weight is on its spec sheet. Choose a rating well above it, and remember that a soundbar bracket adds weight. Never rely on a screen diagonal alone.

A full motion arm puts the TV's weight out from the wall, so it must go into studs or solid masonry. The Pipishell fits 12 in and 16 in studs, and the Amazon Basics works on a single stud. Drywall anchors are not safe for a heavy extended TV. Find the studs first.

The Mounting Dream caps at 400 by 400 mm, the Amazon Basics goes to 15.7 by 15.7 in and the USX starts at 200 by 100 mm. Check the TV's VESA holes against the mount's range. A mismatch cannot be fixed.

The USX swivels 45 degrees each way and tilts +5 to -15, and the others offer similar ranges. The arm's extension determines how far the TV comes out. A long arm adds leverage on the wall. Choose the minimum extension you need.

The ECHOGEAR and Perlegear state a UL listing, while several others do not in the text we reviewed. A UL listing means the mount was evaluated to a safety standard. It does not replace checking your wall. Read the rating line.

The ECHOGEAR provides a drilling template and takes under 30 minutes, the USX and Mounting Dream provide labeled hardware. A TV on an arm is awkward to lift, so use two people. Cables must have slack for the full motion.

specDecoder.watchFor: The Perlegear and USX list 132 lb and the Amazon Basics 80 lb.

howWeEvaluated.title: Listing specifications
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each mount from the TV size, weight limit, VESA range and tilt stated on its Amazon listing. We did not install any of them. The ECHOGEAR's 125 lb and the Perlegear's 132 lb are numbers we compare.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety claims
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted which listings state a UL listing. Where a listing did not, we say so. That is why the ECHOGEAR and Perlegear rank highly.

howWeEvaluated.title: On-topic filtering
howWeEvaluated.description: The topic search returned many near-identical mounts from the same makers and a small-screen mount. We kept one per design family. That left a lineup of six.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered recurring themes such as sag at full extension, creaks and stud-finding errors. We do not repeat ratings or counts. A pattern counted only when it matched the described design.

howWeEvaluated.title: Honest limits
howWeEvaluated.description: Weight limits and UL listings are maker statements. We say so plainly. Install safety depends on your wall and your fasteners.

cards.label: Single-stud arm
cards.text: The Amazon Basics suits small TVs and limited studs. It is simple and less stable at full extension.

cards.label: Dual articulating arms
cards.text: The Perlegear, USX and Pipishell use two arms. They carry heavier TVs and extend further.

howToChoose.note: Choose a dual-arm mount for larger TVs and a simple arm for small ones.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A weight limit well above your TV, a VESA match, a UL listing, a reach that does not overextend and cable slack. Use a stud finder and two people.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The ECHOGEAR and Perlegear both suit living rooms, with the Perlegear higher in rating and the ECHOGEAR more detailed on install.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a motorized mount, a very large TV with a heavy soundbar or a long-reach arm with a lifetime warranty. Those sit above these listings.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The TV is small and light. A simple arm like the Amazon Basics covers that.

maintenance.task: Check bolts and the wall plate
maintenance.interval: After one week, then every 6 months
maintenance.why: Joints settle and screws loosen. Tighten and check the level.
Cables stretch when the arm moves. Leave a loop.
Dust and grit make joints stiff. Wipe and add a drop of light oil if allowed.
Screws can loosen with movement. Tighten them by hand.
Sudden pulls stress the studs. Move the TV slowly and avoid hanging items on it.

faq.q: Do I need studs for a full motion mount?
faq.a: Yes, or solid masonry. A drywall anchor is not safe for an extended TV.

faq.q: What does UL listed mean for a mount?
faq.a: It was evaluated by a safety testing body. It does not replace correct installation.

faq.q: How do I check my TV's VESA pattern?
faq.a: Look in the manual or measure the hole spacing on the back. It must match the mount's range.

faq.q: Can I mount a TV over a fireplace?
faq.a: Only if the wall is solid and the heat is low. Check the wall and the heat before you drill.

faq.q: Is a full motion mount heavy?
faq.a: Yes. Use two people to hang the TV.

faq.q: How far should I extend the arm?
faq.a: As little as you need. A long reach adds leverage and strain on the wall.
